name: Window cleaning
summary: Start a window cleaning business: your first 25 people and partners, prices per window and per pane from real ranges, a window count estimate sheet, a same-street route and a storefront route.
door_hello: Your windows, clear inside and out, no ladder work for you
door_step3: I clean every pane and send before and after photos
door_rule: Hand these out in person, hang them on doorknobs or pin them on community boards. Never put flyers in or on a mailbox (18 U.S. Code 1725).

promises.first_25: 15 people you know and 10 local agents, managers, shops and apartment buildings, each with a message, plus door hangers with the offer that fits the season.
promises.offer: Your prices per window, per pane and per house from real ranges, the first-clients ladder, a storefront route price and job math, on a one-page offer sheet.
promises.quote: Window counts by type, floors, inside or out, screens and tracks in; a per-window quote, a text and an invoice out.
promises.keep: A thank-you, an honest review ask, your spring and fall plan, a referral ask and a later check-in, each dated, plus review cards with your QR code.
promises.sample_one: One front window cleaned free for one street or one partner: a card to send, door hangers or a sample letter, and every message, saved to your Pipeline.
promises.reply: Paste what someone wrote back: what they meant, a short answer with one next step, and your Pipeline updated. A draft you send yourself.
promises.won: Log the yes, then everything for the job: the booking text, a prep text, a printable job sheet with ladder checks, the after-job text and the invoice.
promises.proof: One job turned into proof: a result card, a before-and-after collage from your photos, a caption, an honest review ask and a case study once they say yes.
promises.next_25: The next 25 agents, property managers, shops and apartment buildings near you that are not in your Pipeline yet, each with its messages, saved for Do my day.
promises.ready: Look ready before you reach out: a one-page website, a Google profile kit and a flyer, all from your real prices.
promises.same_street: Turn one customer's street into a route: neighbor door hangers with a lower price, a route sheet to tick off and the intro ask for your customer.
promises.storefronts: Shops and cafes near you in walking order, with a free demo window, a counter script, a rate sheet and directions for each leg.
promises.estimate: Count windows by type and floor: minutes per pane, a price from your per-window and per-pane rates, the gear each floor needs and a printable estimate sheet.

off_season.play: Book spring window cleanings now with a deposit, and keep a storefront route every 2 weeks going through winter.

crowd.note: Spring and fall peaks; slow in winter up north.

items.what_to_check: OSHA's ladder rules bind employers and their workers, and the OSH Act does not cover the self-employed. Follow the ladder rules yourself from day one; all of them apply to anyone you hire. UK guidance says to avoid work at height where you can, with water-fed poles or by cleaning from inside.

sources.says: The employer must ensure ladders are inspected before initial use in each work shift; each employee faces the ladder and uses at least one hand to grasp it when climbing, and carries no object or load that could cause a fall; portable ladders are used only on stable and level surfaces unless secured or stabilized; no ladder is moved while an employee is on it; ladders in passageways, doorways or driveways are secured or barricaded; the cap and top step of a stepladder are not used as steps; ladders are not placed on boxes or barrels for more height.

sources.says: Windows should be cleaned twice per year; avoid sunny days, since sunlight dries the solution too quickly and leaves streaks.
Many people have their windows professionally cleaned once or twice a year.
Residential customers typically need service 2 to 4 times per year; commercial storefronts are $2 to $5 per window on weekly or every-two-weeks contracts.

seasonality.pattern: Inside cleaning is most often booked as a spring or pre-holiday add-on.

sources.says: Many customers book exterior-only service first, which costs about half as much as a full interior and exterior clean; interior cleaning is most common as a seasonal add-on, spring or pre-holiday.

seasonality.pattern: House work is rare in winter where it is cold: keep a storefront route going and book spring work ahead.

sources.says: Some cleaners charge $10 to $30 per unit to remove hard water (calcium or lime) stains; residential washing in winter is rare.

Route density means multiple clients serviced in the same neighborhood on the same day; property managers can be a target for recurring commercial work; operators in colder climates often plan for less winter work or pivot to holiday light installation.

Storefronts are ideal for beginners: quick jobs, frequent service, easy to acquire; start with storefronts: walk in, introduce yourself, offer to clean one window free, and build a route of 20 to 50 weekly stops.

seasonality.pattern: Clean on cloudy days or in the shade when you can: sun dries the solution too fast and leaves streaks.

sources.says: Windows should be cleaned twice per year; avoid sunny days, since sunlight dries the solution too quickly and leaves streaks.

default_costs.basis: Defaults when you leave them empty, all judgment calls: about $15 of solution, towels and blades per job (Fixr puts materials at about $1 to $2 a window), $25 an hour for your time, $150 a month fixed (StartCosts: insurance $80 to $150 and phone and software $30 to $80 a month for a solo operator). Use your own numbers.

sources.says: Of a flat $8 to $16 per window, around 90% is labor ($7 to $14) and about $1 to $2 is materials.

advice.say: Upper floors: work from the ground with a pole, or from inside on tilt-in windows. On a ladder, look for power lines first, use levelers on uneven ground and set the foot out a quarter of the working length (OSHA).
Three stories: leave out any window you can't reach from the ground or from inside until you have the gear, the insurance and the practice.
Storefronts: agree the day and time with the manager and put the route stop in writing.
Inside only is rare: check that the trip minimum covers your drive.

both: Glass inside and out on every window counted
out: Outside glass on every window counted
in: Inside glass on every window counted

floor2.say: Second floor: look for power lines before you raise a ladder and never use a metal ladder near them; set it on firm, level ground with levelers and put the foot out a quarter of the working length.

sources.says: Look for overhead power lines before handling a ladder and avoid a metal ladder near power lines; inspect the ladder before use; keep 3-point contact and face the ladder; use a ladder only on a stable and level surface unless it is secured; ladder levelers only for their designed purpose; don't stand on the three top rungs of a straight or extension ladder; set the base a quarter of the working length from the wall; extend 3 feet above the support; the load rating includes the weight of tools.

A non-self-supporting ladder is set so the foot is about one-quarter of the working length out from the top support; ladders need nonconductive side rails where they could contact energized electrical equipment; the top step of a stepladder is not a step.

floor3.say: Third floor: clean from the ground with a water-fed pole or from inside, and leave out any window you can't reach that way until you have the gear, the insurance and the practice.

sources.says: When planning window cleaning you must avoid work at height where it is reasonably practicable, for example by using telescopic water fed poles or cleaning windows from the inside; health and safety law also applies to self-employed window cleaners (UK law and guidance).

sources.publisher: UK Health and Safety Executive, water-fed pole guide
sources.says: Water-fed pole systems clean windows up to 80 ft (24 m) high from ground level and remove the need to work at height; don't use a water-fed pole near overhead power lines, and treat the pole as potentially conductive.
Charge more for every floor past the first, or if you're spending extra time to set up safely; anything above the second floor is a hazard and a hassle.

skylight.say: Skylights: clean them from inside, and the roof side only from the ground with a pole. Stay off the roof.

sources.says: When planning window cleaning you must avoid work at height where it is reasonably practicable, for example by using telescopic water fed poles or cleaning windows from the inside; health and safety law also applies to self-employed window cleaners (UK law and guidance).

hard_water.say: Hard water spots: test one window first and show the customer before you do the rest.

sources.says: Screen cleaning $2 to $5 per screen; track detailing $2 to $5 per window; hard-water stain removal $10 to $30 per window; skylights $20 to $30 each.

inside_only.say: Inside only is rare: check that the trip minimum covers your drive.

sources.says: Exterior washing $6.40 to $12.80 and interior $1.60 to $3.20 per window; exterior is usually about 80% of the in-and-out price; it is rare to have interior-only washing.
